name: 👑 Anaxandridas II
party: year-level backbone — Agiad mainline; Sparta had a dual kingship — a Eurypontid king (Ariston in this period) always reigned concurrently

name: 👑 Cleomenes I
party: year-level backbone — dual kingship: concurrent Eurypontid kings Demaratus, then Leotychidas II

name: 👑 Leonidas I
party: year-level backbone — fell at Thermopylae, 480 BC; concurrent Eurypontid king Leotychidas II

name: 👑 Pleistarchus
party: year-level backbone — dual kingship: concurrent Eurypontid king Archidamus II (r. 469/8–427/6)

name: 👑 Pleistoanax
party: year-level backbone — reign interrupted by exile c. 445–427; concurrent Eurypontid kings Archidamus II and Agis II

name: 👑 Pausanias
party: year-level backbone — exiled 395; concurrent Eurypontid kings Agis II, then Agesilaus II (r. c. 400–360)

name: 👑 Agesipolis I
party: year-level backbone — dual kingship: concurrent Eurypontid king Agesilaus II

name: 👑 Cleombrotus I
party: year-level backbone — killed at Leuctra, 371 BC; concurrent Eurypontid king Agesilaus II

name: 👑 Agesipolis II
party: year-level backbone — brief reign; concurrent Eurypontid king Agesilaus II

name: 👑 Cleomenes II
party: year-level backbone — longest attested Agiad reign; concurrent Eurypontid kings Agesilaus II through Eudamidas I

name: 👑 Areus I
party: year-level backbone — dual kingship maintained with the Eurypontid line

name: 👑 Acrotatus
party: year-level backbone — son of Areus I; dual kingship maintained

name: 👑 Areus II
party: year-level backbone — child king; dual kingship maintained

name: 👑 Leonidas II
party: year-level backbone — briefly deposed in favour of Cleombrotus II (242–241); concurrent Eurypontid king Agis IV among others

name: 👑 Cleomenes III
party: year-level backbone — revolutionary reformer; abolished the traditional dual kingship in practice; defeated at Sellasia and fled, 222 BC

name: 👑 Agesipolis III
party: year-level backbone — gap 222–219 BC (no kings after Sellasia); last Agiad king, dethroned by the Eurypontid Lycurgus in 215

name: 👑 Nabis
party: year-level backbone — gap 215–207 BC (Eurypontid Lycurgus, then the regent Machanidas); Nabis, of Eurypontid-era descent claimed, ruled as tyrant/king — last ruler of independent Sparta, killed 192 BC
